sections.assessment_and_plan: Assessment: Admitted for evaluation and management of: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea. Working diagnosis: acute myocardial infarction (severity: severe). Comorbidities: Chronic ischemic heart disease (IHD), Hypertension (HTN), Dyslipidemia. Plan: Estimated length of stay: ~7 days. Initial medications: Aspirin, Ticagrelor, Heparin, Nitroglycerin. Workup / procedures: Arterial line insertion, Transthoracic echocardiography. Planned procedures: Urinary catheter insertion, Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Admission work-up: CBC, coagulation studies, LFT, lipid panel, troponin I, troponin I (6 h repeat), CK-MB, BNP, 12-lead ECG, echocardiogram, coronary angiography, chest X-ray AP. Supportive care and monitoring: O2: Nasal cannula SpO2 >= 94%, IV access: Two large-bore peripheral IVs, continuous monitoring: Continuous ECG telemetry, BP q15min x 4h then q1h, bed rest: Bed rest for initial 12-24h, NPO: NPO until catheterization assessment.

sections.admission_summary: Chief complaint: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea. Admitted for inpatient care.
sections.discharge_instructions: Drink plenty of fluids. Get adequate rest and avoid overexertion. Cardiology follow-up within 1-2 weeks. Cardiac rehabilitation enrollment recommended. Take your heart medications (Aspirin, Ticagrelor, Atorvastatin) every day as prescribed. Do NOT stop them without consulting your cardiologist. Call 911 immediately for: chest pain, severe shortness of breath, palpitations, syncope. Resume a normal diet gradually as tolerated. Restricted activity for 4-6 weeks. Avoid heavy lifting. Gradual return per cardiologist guidance. Call ambulance immediately for chest pain lasting >15 min, dyspnea, syncope, or cold sweats. Low-fat, low-sodium diet. Weight management.
sections.discharge_medications: Aspirin 81mg PO daily x365d; Ticagrelor 90mg PO BID x365d; Atorvastatin 80mg PO daily x365d
sections.follow_up: Cardiology follow-up within 1-2 weeks. Cardiac rehabilitation enrollment recommended.
sections.hospital_course: Length of stay: 14 days (primary reason: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea). Main treatment: vasoactive drugs (Dobutamine); antithrombotic therapy (Heparin, Aspirin, Ticagrelor); other parenteral drugs (Nitroglycerin). Key procedures: Urinary catheter insertion (2024-06-15), Arterial line insertion (2024-06-15), Transthoracic echocardiography (2024-06-15), Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (2024-06-15). Significant results: troponin I 97.881 ng/mL [H] (troponin elevation) on hospital day 1. Medication changes from admission: started Aspirin, Ticagrelor, Atorvastatin. Condition at discharge: discharged to skilled nursing facility, Barthel Index 95/100.

sections.adl_assessment: Barthel Index 60/100 → moderate assistance (Feeding 5, Bathing 5, Mobility 10, Toilet use 5)
sections.care_plan: Care plan: Nursing problem: acute pain (chest pain). Goal: Chest pain resolves and the activity level can be widened with stable hemodynamics and ECG. Observation: Observe the site, severity and duration of chest pain; check ECG monitor, vital signs and urine output; Watch for diaphoresis, dyspnea or altered consciousness with chest symptoms. Care: Keep the ordered activity level and mobilize stepwise as the cardiac rehabilitation plan allows; Give ordered analgesia for pain and check its effect.
